searches.note: Seventeen searches of twenty eight, eleven unspent. Two were restricted to a house's own domain (millton.co.nz, lindauer.co.nz) and one to matawhero.co.nz with Rural News and Raymond Chan; they are read as primary through their summaries. Others blocked the author's main sources so the second source would be independent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label words, every beat of the story, cards and questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was in one source only, or none, it was cut or said with less.

Writers' own sites met among the results (Wine with Seth, Wine Anorak, Vinography, Raymond Chan Wine Reviews, Celia Hay) are not cited in the fragment as a second source; the author's Vinography source was cut.

tested: Founding of 1984 on the Te Arai River near Manutuke: the house's history page and Rural News. Sound.
Opou planted in 1969 by the father of one founder: Wine Anorak, Grokipedia and the house; replanted 1983. The parents, the sheep station and the 1984 handover not found. Changed.
BioGro certification of 1989 as the country's first: the house (first organic and biodynamic wine estate), Rural News (first grape land to gain BioGro). Sound. Demeter year: 1990 or 2009. Left out.
Hand picking in passes and botrytis from the river's autumn mists: the house's notes of 2025 (three selections), an older listing (up to four), the 2007 note. Changed to up to four.
Demi-muids of 600 litres beside steel: bottlebooks and a merchant's note. Sound, reworded.
Retirement and last harvest of 2025: Vino Fino and Advintage quoting the family, 41 vintages. Sound, the last harvest added.

swaps.why: Vinoptima went into receivership in 2018, was sold and its Gewürztraminer vines were reported pulled out in 2022 (NZ Herald, The Country); the plan's own note says drop the pick if it no longer makes the wine. A guest will not meet a new Ormond Reserve.
swaps.to: Bushmere Estate, flagship its Chardonnay (Classic Chardonnay on the label as met in one review), recommended: New Zealand Winegrowers' own winery listing gives Chardonnay planted in 1972 on the estate, with Montepulciano planted by a mislabelling; Cuisine gives its own label from 2004 or 2005 after grape contracts ended. Kirkpatrick Estate of the Patutahi Plateau is the second choice, its founding year (2003) in one directory only. Either needs its own author and refuter before it stands.

swaps.why: The brand's own Classic Brut page gives South Australian fruit, its method is unsettled, and its Gisborne tie is history (the winery Indevin took in 2010). The flagship no longer speaks for Gisborne.
swaps.to: Kirkpatrick Estate of Patutahi, or another Gisborne grower's label, at the read together agent's choice; if Bushmere takes Vinoptima's place, Kirkpatrick takes this one. If the agent prefers to keep a sparkling voice, the Lindauer Special Reserve Brut Cuvée, which the brand gives as Gisborne and Hawke's Bay and bottle fermented, would be the honest pick, but it is still a brand of Lion's, not a Gisborne house.
